title: Shadow scoring: async queue + worker (retries, dedupe, DLQ) for quality metrics
creator: Nadia Rahman
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Overview
We need an asynchronous scoring pipeline that computes rubric/heuristic quality metrics for shadow outputs without impacting the user request path. This ticket covers the queue + worker subsystem responsible for: (1) consuming shadow pair artifacts (control + shadow outputs + metadata), (2) running scoring (heuristics + model-graded via eval-harness adapter), (3) writing normalized results for aggregation in Console, and (4) providing reliability mechanisms (retries, dedupe, DLQ, backpressure).

Goals / requirements
- Fail-open: scoring must never block or degrade the user path; if scoring is unhealthy we drop/defer scoring work and surface “data incomplete / scoring lag” signals.
- Idempotent + deduped processing: replays and telemetry retries are expected. We must prevent duplicate scoring writes and avoid double-counting in aggregates.
- Cost-guarded: enforce per-tenant and global budgets (QPS, concurrency, max tokens graded). Worker should degrade to cheaper heuristics when budgets are exceeded (configurable).
- Multi-deployment aware:
  - Hosted/Dedicated: managed queue + workers in Redwood infra.
  - Private: support running the worker near the data; allow alternative sinks/queues; default minimal retention and strict redaction handling.

Non-goals
- Customer-provided arbitrary code execution (v1 only runs Redwood scoring templates + eval-harness rubrics).
- Long-term offline replay of historical traffic beyond short retention windows.

Proposed architecture (v1)
1) Input
- Source events: shadow_pair_completed (from ENG-5404 telemetry ingestion) emits a scoring job referencing stored artifacts.
- We do NOT ship raw prompts/responses directly through the queue by default; instead we pass artifact refs + hashed identifiers.

2) Queue
- Topic/queue name (proposed): shadow.scoring.jobs.v1
- Partition key: tenant_id (to keep noisy tenants isolated and enable per-tenant concurrency controls)
- Payload fields (high level): tenant_id, shadow_experiment_id, route_id, control_variant_id, shadow_variant_id, request_fingerprint, artifact_ref, rubric_version, created_at, attempt

3) Worker service
- Service name (proposed): shadow-scoring-worker
- Reads from shadow.scoring.jobs.v1, fetches artifacts, runs scoring, writes results.
- Scoring modes:
  - Heuristics: format adherence, JSON validity/shape, refusal detection, length/verbosity deltas.
  - Model-graded: uses eval-harness adapter (ENG-5406) with pinned rubric_version.
- Output table (logical): shadow_scoring_results_v1 keyed by (tenant_id, shadow_experiment_id, request_fingerprint, shadow_variant_id, rubric_version)

4) Dedupe / idempotency
- Dedupe key: tenant_id + shadow_experiment_id + request_fingerprint + shadow_variant_id + rubric_version
- Implementation:
  - First write creates a result row with status=completed and a stable score_hash.
  - Retries check for existing completed row; if present, ACK and stop.
  - For in-flight duplicates: use “insert if not exists” semantics or optimistic concurrency on status.

5) Retries + DLQ
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max_attempts=6 (configurable).
- Failure classes:
  - Transient: artifact store timeouts, eval-harness timeouts, upstream rate limiting -> retry.
  - Permanent: malformed artifact refs, missing required fields, rubric version not found -> DLQ.
- DLQ topic/queue: shadow.scoring.jobs.dlq.v1 with structured error reason, last_attempt_at.

6) Backpressure and circuit breaking
- If scoring backlog exceeds threshold (see SLOs), worker reduces concurrency and/or skips model-graded scoring and emits “scoring_degraded=true” signals.
- If artifact fetch p99 latency spikes, circuit-break artifact store calls to avoid cascading failures.

7) Observability
- Metrics:
  - shadow_scoring_jobs_received_total
  - shadow_scoring_jobs_completed_total
  - shadow_scoring_jobs_failed_total (by error_class)
  - shadow_scoring_queue_lag_seconds (p50/p95)
  - shadow_scoring_worker_latency_ms (end-to-end, plus artifact_fetch, eval_harness, write)
  - shadow_scoring_dedupe_hits_total
  - shadow_scoring_degraded_mode_total
- Tracing: propagate request_fingerprint + experiment_id as trace attributes (cardinality-safe; do not include raw prompt_id).

SLO targets (draft; to finalize with SRE)
- Availability: worker processes >= 99.0% of valid jobs within the scoring window.
- Freshness: p95 end-to-end scoring latency <= 10 minutes (from shadow_pair_completed to result write) for default sampling rates.
- Backlog: alert when p95 queue lag > 30 minutes for 15 minutes.

Security / data handling
- Worker must only fetch artifacts that have passed redaction/transformation (ENG-5411).
- Ensure all logs redact artifact contents; log only hashed identifiers.
- RBAC: results are tenant-scoped; do not allow cross-tenant reads.

Acceptance criteria
- Queue + worker deployed behind feature flag (shadow_scoring_v1).
- Dedupe works: repeated job delivery does not create multiple scoring result rows or inflate aggregates.
- Retries + DLQ: transient failures recover; permanent failures land in DLQ with actionable error classification.
- Degraded mode: when queue lag threshold is crossed, model-graded scoring can be disabled automatically and the system continues to produce heuristic metrics and “data incomplete” markers.
- Observability dashboards show queue lag, throughput, error rates, and degraded-mode activations.
- Load test demonstrates no material impact to user path SLOs (no coupling) and stable behavior at projected beta sampling.

Implementation plan (current)
- [x] Define job envelope schema + versioning
- [x] Stand up queue topic + IAM/RBAC for worker
- [x] Implement worker skeleton: consume -> fetch artifact -> score -> write result
- [x] Idempotent write path + dedupe key
- [x] Retry wrapper + error classification
- [ ] DLQ routing + triage runbook stub
- [ ] Degraded-mode toggle + per-tenant budget caps
- [ ] Metrics + dashboards + alert hooks for lag/errors
- [ ] Private deployment notes (queue abstraction + storage options)

Links
- Related: ENG-5404 (telemetry events), ENG-5406 (eval-harness adapter), ENG-5411 (retention/redaction), ENG-5415 (backpressure/circuit breaker)
- GitHub: eval-harness/pr-812-shadow-output-adapter-and-rubric-runner (dependency)
- Incident learning: scoring queue backlog during dogfood (see Slack: incidents/1768180020-shadow-scoring-queue-backlog)

Open questions
1) Do we require rubric_version in the job payload, or can worker resolve via experiment config? (Leaning: include rubric_version to guarantee reproducibility and allow replays.)
2) Default timeouts for model-graded scoring per job (proposal: hard timeout 20s for worker step; retry at most 2x for model-graded before falling back to heuristics).
3) Storage schema ownership: keep results in telemetry warehouse vs product DB for Console queries? (Leaning: write normalized results to analytics store, with a thin index in product DB for “experiment run state”.)
4) Private deployments: do we support running scoring without GPU (heuristics-only) as default? (Likely yes for v1; model-graded optional if customer provisions.)
